name: Kestrel
oneLiner: Read your service logs in a browser, on the machine that wrote them.
paragraph: Kestrel tails the log files you point it at and serves them as a searchable page on localhost. It reads the files in place: there is no agent to install, no index to build and nothing is uploaded. Filters are saved per folder in a plain JSON file beside the logs. It is for one person on one machine, and it has no authentication, so keep it on localhost.
audience: A developer who runs a handful of services locally and already reads their logs with tail and grep. They know what a log level and a regex are. They need to know which files Kestrel opens, that it never writes to them, and that it listens on localhost only.
notThis: Not a log shipper or a hosted log service.
Not a metrics or tracing tool.
Not safe to expose beyond localhost.

pillars.name: Calm
pillars.means: No superlatives, no urgency, no exclamation marks.

pillars.name: Concrete
pillars.means: Name the file, the port, the command, the count.

pillars.name: Candid
pillars.means: State the limit next to the feature.
pillars.prevents: A feature list with no edges

visual.colorway: Near-monochrome. One amber accent, spent on the primary action and the live indicator only. Light by default, with a complete dark theme.
visual.typography: Inter for text and the wordmark (lowercase, weight 640, tight tracking). JetBrains Mono for log lines and commands.

project.demoNotes: Point it at the sample logs with KESTREL_DIR=./fixtures/logs before npm run dev.

social.audience: Developers who run services locally and read logs in a terminal; they read Hacker News and Mastodon.
